name: Hang shelves level
blurb: Marking out, choosing the right fixings for the wall type, and getting it level — a shelf that sags or tilts is a permanent daily annoyance.
gear: A spirit level or laser level
steps: Decide the height and mark a level line across the wall with a spirit level, checking it in both directions.
Identify the wall type: solid masonry needs plugs, plasterboard needs cavity anchors or a stud.
Locate studs, or choose cavity fixings rated well above the intended load.
Mark the bracket holes off the level line, not off the previous bracket — errors compound.
Drill, plug and fix the first bracket loosely, then use the level across to position the second before tightening both.
Fit the shelf, check level again, and load it gradually to test.
tips: Floors and ceilings in most houses are not level. Never use them as a reference.
Match fixing to load. Plasterboard plugs pull out under book weight surprisingly easily.
proof: A loaded shelf that reads level in both directions and does not move when you lean on it.
